name: Mars
description: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest in the Solar System. Known as the Red Planet due to its iron oxide (rust) surface, Mars hosts the tallest volcano (Olympus Mons) and longest canyon (Valles Marineris) in the Solar System. It is the most explored planet beyond Earth.
surface: Red iron oxide plains, polar ice caps, ancient river valleys, volcanic regions
largest_volcano: Olympus Mons — 21,171 m tall, 624 km wide
largest_canyon: Valles Marineris — 4,000 km long, 200 km wide, 7 km deep
magnetic_field: No global field (remnant crustal magnetism only)
summary: Mars is humanity's most studied neighboring planet and prime candidate for future human colonization. Despite a harsh thin atmosphere and extreme cold, Mars shows compelling evidence of ancient liquid water — river valleys, lake beds, and minerals that form in water. Current rovers and orbiters are searching for signs of past microbial life.
interesting_facts: Olympus Mons is the tallest volcano in the Solar System at 21 km — 3× Mount Everest
Valles Marineris is as long as the distance from New York to Los Angeles
A Martian day (sol) is 24 hours and 37 minutes — remarkably similar to Earth
Mars has two small, potato-shaped moons: Phobos and Deimos (captured asteroids)
Perseverance produced oxygen from Martian CO₂ in 2021 using the MOXIE experiment
Ingenuity helicopter made the first powered flight on another planet in April 2021
Mars has the largest dust storms in the Solar System, sometimes covering the entire planet
Ancient Mars had liquid water — evidence includes river delta deposits in Jezero Crater
Phobos orbits Mars faster than Mars rotates — it rises in the west and sets in the east
SpaceX plans to send humans to Mars in the early 2030s

faq.q: Why is Mars called the Red Planet?
faq.a: Mars appears red due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface. The iron in Martian soil oxidized billions of years ago, coating the rocks and dust in a reddish hue.

Not without significant technology. Mars has no breathable oxygen, temperatures as low as -125°C, deadly radiation (no magnetic field), and only 38% of Earth's gravity. Future habitats would need life support systems.
Mars has water ice at its poles and underground. Ancient Mars had liquid water — evidence includes river valleys, lake beds in Jezero Crater, and water-formed minerals found by rovers.

faq.q: How many rovers are on Mars?
faq.a: As of 2024: Curiosity (NASA, active since 2012) and Perseverance (NASA, active since 2021). China's Zhurong rover (2021) has ceased operations. Opportunity operated 2004–2018.

Olympus Mons is the largest volcano in the Solar System, 21,171 m tall (nearly 3× Mount Everest) and 624 km wide. It formed over billions of years of volcanic activity without plate tectonics moving the crust.

faq.q: How long does it take to get to Mars?
faq.a: A spacecraft takes about 7–9 months to travel from Earth to Mars, depending on the relative positions of the planets. Mars and Earth are closest (54.6 million km) every ~26 months.

Ingenuity is NASA's small robotic helicopter that arrived with Perseverance in 2021. It made the first powered flight on another planet in April 2021 and completed 72 flights before communications ended in early 2024.

faq.q: How many moons does Mars have?
faq.a: Mars has two small moons: Phobos (27 km wide) and Deimos (15 km wide). Both are believed to be captured asteroids from the asteroid belt.

Perseverance is searching for signs of ancient microbial life in Jezero Crater (an ancient lake bed), collecting rock samples for eventual return to Earth, and testing technologies for future human missions.
Mars has been known since antiquity — ancient Egyptians, Babylonians, and Greeks all observed it. The Roman name 'Mars' (god of war) comes from its blood-red color.
